questions.sec: MEN syndromes and MEN1 · p858
questions.q: The MEN types listed are:
questions.exp: Types: MEN 1, MEN 2A, MEN 2B/MEN 3, MEN 4. (Book p858)

questions.sec: MEN syndromes and MEN1 · p858
questions.q: MEN1 inheritance and sex ratio are:
questions.exp: MEN1 is autosomal dominant with M = F. (Book p858)

questions.sec: MEN syndromes and MEN1 · p858
questions.q: MEN1 is caused by mutation of the ___ gene (tumour suppressor) on chromosome 11q.
questions.exp: MENIN gene (tumour suppressor) mutation on Chr 11q; d/t intron inversion > base pair deletion. (Book p858)

questions.sec: MEN syndromes and MEN1 · p858
questions.q: The mutation mechanism in MEN1 is typically:
questions.exp: D/t intron inversion > base pair deletion. (Book p858)

questions.sec: MEN syndromes and MEN1 · p858
questions.q: Match the MEN1 major ‘3P’ involvement with frequency — 1) Parathyroid  2) Pancreas  3) Pituitary … A) 50–70%  B) 30–50%  C) 100%
questions.exp: Major (age <20 yrs) 3P: parathyroid 100%, pancreas 50–70%, pituitary 30–50%. (Book p858)

questions.sec: MEN syndromes and MEN1 · p858
questions.q: The MEN1 minor skin lesions in order are:
questions.exp: Skin minor manifestations: angiofibroma > collagenoma > lipoma. (Book p858)

questions.sec: MEN syndromes and MEN1 · p858
questions.q: The m/c benign minor tumour and the m/c neurotumour in MEN1 are respectively:
questions.exp: Benign minor tumours: adreno-cortical adenoma (m/c), meningioma (m/c neurotumour), pheochromocytoma (<1%). (Book p858)

questions.sec: MEN syndromes and MEN1 · p858
questions.q: The malignant minor tumours of MEN1 are:
questions.exp: Malignant minor: primitive neuro-ectodermal tumour (PNET), thymic & foregut carcinoid. (Book p858)

questions.sec: MEN1 organ details: parathyroid, pancreas, pituitary and MEN2A gene · p859
questions.q: Match MEN1 vs sporadic primary hyperparathyroidism — 1) MEN1 cause  2) Sporadic cause  3) MEN1 age  4) Sporadic age … A) Females >40 yrs (peak 60)  B) Asymmetric hyperplasia  C) <20 yrs  D) Adenoma
questions.exp: MEN1: asymmetric hyperplasia, <20 yrs, M=F; sporadic: adenoma, females >40 (peak 60), F>>>M. (Book p859)

questions.sec: MEN1 organ details: parathyroid, pancreas, pituitary and MEN2A gene · p859
questions.q: The IOC for localising hyperparathyroidism (both MEN1 and sporadic) is:
questions.exp: IOC = 99m Tc sestamibi scan. (Book p859)

questions.sec: MEN1 organ details: parathyroid, pancreas, pituitary and MEN2A gene · p859
questions.q: The surgical treatment for MEN1-associated hyperparathyroidism is:
questions.exp: Treatment: 3 1/2 near-total parathyroidectomy (MEN1); adenoid extension for sporadic. (Book p859)

questions.sec: MEN1 organ details: parathyroid, pancreas, pituitary and MEN2A gene · p859
questions.q: The m/c symptom of hypercalcaemia overall is:
questions.exp: Note: m/c symptom of hypercalcaemia overall = fatigue. (Book p859)

questions.sec: MEN1 organ details: parathyroid, pancreas, pituitary and MEN2A gene · p859
questions.q: The m/c cause of death in MEN1 is:
questions.exp: Enteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumour is the m/c cause of death in MEN1. (Book p859)

questions.sec: MEN1 organ details: parathyroid, pancreas, pituitary and MEN2A gene · p859
questions.q: The enteropancreatic tumour frequency order in MEN1 is:
questions.exp: Gastrinoma > insulinoma > glucagonoma > VIPoma (20–40 yrs). (Book p859)

questions.sec: MEN1 organ details: parathyroid, pancreas, pituitary and MEN2A gene · p859
questions.q: Glucagonoma is associated with which rash?
questions.exp: Glucagonoma: migratory necrolytic erythematous rash. (Book p859)

questions.sec: MEN1 organ details: parathyroid, pancreas, pituitary and MEN2A gene · p859
questions.q: VIPoma causes the ___ syndrome (watery diarrhoea, hypochlorhydria, acidosis).
questions.exp: WDHA syndrome with a normal anion gap metabolic acidosis (NAGMA). (Book p859)

questions.sec: MEN1 organ details: parathyroid, pancreas, pituitary and MEN2A gene · p859
questions.q: Match gastrinoma features MEN1 vs sporadic — 1) MEN1 location  2) Sporadic location  3) MEN1 malignancy risk  4) Sporadic malignancy risk … A) Passaro's triangle  B) <5%  C) Duodenum  D) >50–60%
questions.exp: MEN1 gastrinoma: duodenum, small multifocal, <5% malignant, IOC endoscopic US, spreads by lymph node; sporadic: Passaro's triangle, large, >50–60%, SRS scan, blood stream. (Book p859)

questions.sec: MEN1 organ details: parathyroid, pancreas, pituitary and MEN2A gene · p859
questions.q: Match gastrinoma IOC — 1) MEN1-associated  2) Sporadic … A) Somatostatin receptor scintigraphy (SRS) scan  B) Endoscopic ultrasound
questions.exp: MEN1 gastrinoma IOC = endoscopic ultrasound; sporadic = SRS scan; treatment streptozocin + octreotide vs high-dose PPI; size >2 cm → surgery. (Book p859)

questions.sec: MEN1 organ details: parathyroid, pancreas, pituitary and MEN2A gene · p859
questions.q: The pituitary tumour of MEN1 is typically:
questions.exp: Pituitary: prolactinoma, aggressive macroadenomas. (Book p859)

questions.sec: MEN1 organ details: parathyroid, pancreas, pituitary and MEN2A gene · p859
questions.q: MEN2A is caused by mutation of the ___ gene (proto-oncogene) on chromosome 10q via point mutation.
questions.exp: RET gene (proto-oncogene) mutation on Chr 10q (d/t point mutation). (Book p859)

questions.sec: MEN2A variants, MEN2B/MEN3 and MEN4 · p860
questions.q: Match classical MEN2A frequencies — 1) Medullary thyroid cancer  2) Pheochromocytoma  3) Parathyroid hyperplasia … A) 50%  B) 25%  C) 100%
questions.exp: Classical MEN2A: MTC 100% + pheochromocytoma 50% + parathyroid hyperplasia 25%. (Book p860)

questions.sec: MEN2A variants, MEN2B/MEN3 and MEN4 · p860
questions.q: The MEN2A variants listed are classical MEN2A plus:
opts: Cutaneous lichen amyloidosis, Hirschsprung's disease, and FMTC
questions.exp: Variants: MEN2A + cutaneous lichen amyloidosis; MEN2A + Hirschsprung's disease; familial medullary thyroid cancer (FMTC). (Book p860)

questions.sec: MEN2A variants, MEN2B/MEN3 and MEN4 · p860
questions.q: MEN2B/MEN3 combines medullary thyroid carcinoma (100%) and pheochromocytoma (50%) with:
opts: Marfanoid habitus, mucosal & intestinal ganglioneuromatosis, myelinated corneal nerve fibres
questions.exp: MEN2B/MEN3: marfanoid habitus, mucosal & intestinal ganglioneuromatosis, myelinated corneal nerve fibres. (Book p860)

questions.sec: MEN2A variants, MEN2B/MEN3 and MEN4 · p860
questions.q: The tongue image on p860 illustrates:
questions.exp: The photograph shows mucosal ganglioneuromatosis of the tongue. (Book p860)

questions.sec: MEN2A variants, MEN2B/MEN3 and MEN4 · p860
questions.q: MEN4 is caused by mutation of ___.
questions.exp: MEN4 = CDKN1B (cyclin-dependent kinase 1B) mutation. (Book p860)

questions.sec: MEN2A variants, MEN2B/MEN3 and MEN4 · p860
questions.q: MEN4 manifestations include parathyroid hyperplasia (adenoma), pituitary and:
questions.exp: MEN4: parathyroid hyperplasia (adenoma) + pituitary + renal/adrenal tumours + testicular/ovarian tumours. (Book p860)

questions.sec: Phakomatosis/syndrome table and Carney's triad · p861
questions.q: Match syndrome to gene — 1) Hyperparathyroidism/jaw tumour  2) Carney's complex  3) VHL  4) NF1  5) Cowden … A) Neurofibromin (Chr 17)  B) PTEN  C) Parafibromin (CDC73)  D) PRKAR1A  E) VHL gene (Chr 3)
questions.exp: Parafibromin (CDC73), PRKAR1A, VHL (Chr 3), neurofibromin (Chr 17), PTEN respectively; McCune-Albright = post-zygotic GNAS (Gs α). (Book p861)

questions.sec: Phakomatosis/syndrome table and Carney's triad · p861
questions.q: McCune-Albright syndrome differs from the others in inheritance because it is:
opts: Not inherited — post-zygotic GNAS (Gs α protein) mutation
questions.exp: Not inherited; post-zygotic mutation of GNAS gene (Gs α protein). (Book p861)

questions.sec: Phakomatosis/syndrome table and Carney's triad · p861
questions.q: The jaw neoplasia of hyperparathyroidism/jaw tumour syndrome and its endocrine tumour are:
opts: Ossifying fibroma of jaw; parathyroid Ca
questions.exp: Ossifying fibroma of jaw with parathyroid carcinoma. (Book p861)

questions.sec: Phakomatosis/syndrome table and Carney's triad · p861
questions.q: Carney's complex neoplasia and endocrine features are:
opts: Atrial myxoma (lepidic pattern); PPNAD (thin Cushing's), GH adenoma, rare prolactin tumour
questions.exp: Atrial myxoma (lepidic pattern); endocrine PPNAD (thin Cushing's), GH-secreting adenoma, prolactin-secreting tumour (rare); skin lentigenes. (Book p861)

questions.sec: Phakomatosis/syndrome table and Carney's triad · p861
questions.q: The VHL neoplasia list includes renal cell carcinoma, cerebellar haemangioblastoma, islet cell tumours and:
opts: Optic nerve sheath tumour and meningioma
Papillary cystadenoma of broad ligament, epididymal cyst, endolymphatic sac tumours
questions.exp: VHL neoplasia: RCC, cerebellar haemangioblastoma, islet cell tumours, papillary cystadenoma of broad ligament of uterus, epididymal cyst, endolymphatic sac tumours; endocrine pheochromocytoma; additional pancreatic cysts. (Book p861)

questions.sec: Phakomatosis/syndrome table and Carney's triad · p861
questions.q: NF1's neoplasia and endocrine association are:
opts: Optic nerve sheath tumour > meningioma; pheochromocytoma (U/L)
questions.exp: NF1: optic nerve sheath tumour > meningioma; endocrine pheochromocytoma (unilateral). (Book p861)

questions.sec: Phakomatosis/syndrome table and Carney's triad · p861
questions.q: Cowden syndrome (PTEN) neoplasia and thyroid features are:
opts: Ca breast and hamartomatous GIT polyps; nodular goitre or Hashimoto's thyroiditis
questions.exp: Cowden: Ca breast, hamartomatous polyps of GIT; thyroid nodular goitre or Hashimoto's thyroiditis. (Book p861)

questions.sec: Phakomatosis/syndrome table and Carney's triad · p861
questions.q: The McCune-Albright additional-feature triad is:
opts: Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, precocious puberty, café-au-lait spots
questions.exp: Triad: PFD, precocious puberty, café-au-lait spots; endocrine Cushing's, GH-secreting adenoma, precocious puberty. (Book p861)

questions.sec: Phakomatosis/syndrome table and Carney's triad · p861
questions.q: Carney's TRIAD (distinct from Carney's complex) is:
questions.exp: Carney's triad: pulmonary chondroma, GIST, paraganglioma. (Book p861)

questions.sec: RCC comparisons, Cushing's m/c cause by age and the APS table · p862
questions.q: Match RCC behaviour — 1) VHL-associated RCC  2) Sporadic RCC … A) U/L, elderly, blood-stream spread  B) B/L, young (M = F), lymphatic spread
questions.exp: VHL RCC: B/L, young (M=F), lymphatic spread; sporadic: U/L, elderly, blood-stream spread. (Book p862)

questions.sec: RCC comparisons, Cushing's m/c cause by age and the APS table · p862
questions.q: Match tuberous sclerosis vs VHL — 1) TS cysts  2) VHL cysts (m/c)  3) TS renal carcinoma  4) VHL renal carcinoma … A) RCC  B) Cyst in pancreas  C) Cysts in kidney +  D) Angiomyolipoma
questions.exp: TS: kidney cysts + angiomyolipoma; VHL: pancreatic cysts (m/c) + RCC. (Book p862)

questions.sec: RCC comparisons, Cushing's m/c cause by age and the APS table · p862
questions.q: Match the m/c cause of Cushing's syndrome by age — 1) Adults  2) Infants  3) Toddlers … A) McCune-Albright syndrome  B) Adrenocortical carcinoma  C) Pituitary adenoma
questions.exp: Adults: pituitary adenoma; infants: McCune-Albright; toddlers: adrenocortical carcinoma. (Book p862)

questions.sec: RCC comparisons, Cushing's m/c cause by age and the APS table · p862
questions.q: Polyglandular autoimmune syndrome is a.k.a.:
questions.exp: PGA = autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome (APS). (Book p862)

questions.sec: RCC comparisons, Cushing's m/c cause by age and the APS table · p862
questions.q: Match APS type 1 vs type 2 — 1) APS1 age  2) APS2 age  3) APS1 inheritance  4) APS2 inheritance … A) Adult  B) Childhood  C) Polygenic  D) AR
questions.exp: APS1: childhood, M=F, AR; APS2: adult, F>M, polygenic. (Book p862)

questions.sec: RCC comparisons, Cushing's m/c cause by age and the APS table · p862
questions.q: APS type 1 is associated with the ___ gene (AIRE), giving autoimmune poly-endocrinopathy with candidiasis & ectodermal dystrophy.
questions.exp: APECED gene/AIRE; APS2 with HLA DR3 and DR4. (Book p862)

questions.sec: RCC comparisons, Cushing's m/c cause by age and the APS table · p862
questions.q: Autoantibodies in APS1 (besides anti-21-hydroxylase) include:
questions.exp: APS1: anti-21 hydroxylase (Addison's) and anti-interferon antibody; APS2: anti-21 hydroxylase. (Book p862)

questions.sec: RCC comparisons, Cushing's m/c cause by age and the APS table · p862
questions.q: Skin & nail changes are positive in:
questions.exp: Skin & nail changes + in APS1, − in APS2; APS1 adds candidiasis, APS2 associates with coeliac disease. (Book p862)

questions.sec: RCC comparisons, Cushing's m/c cause by age and the APS table · p862
questions.q: Match major thyroid manifestations — 1) APS1  2) APS2 … A) Hashimoto's > Graves  B) Graves > Hashimoto's (with hypoparathyroidism in APS1)
questions.exp: APS1: Graves > Hashimoto's plus hypoparathyroidism and Addison's; APS2: Hashimoto's > Graves with Addison's. Minor (both): type 1 DM, hypogonadism. (Book p862)

questions.sec: RCC comparisons, Cushing's m/c cause by age and the APS table · p862
questions.q: The additional feature distinguishing APS1 from APS2 is:
opts: Candidiasis in APS1; coeliac disease association in APS2
Coeliac in APS1; candidiasis in APS2
questions.exp: APS1 additional = candidiasis; APS2 associated with coeliac disease. (Book p862)

units.title: MEN1: gene, 3P majors and minor tumours
units.guide: MEN types 1, 2A, 2B/3, 4. MEN1 AD, M=F, MENIN (tumour suppressor, 11q), intron inversion > base-pair deletion. Major <20 yrs 3P: parathyroid 100%, pancreas 50–70%, pituitary 30–50%. Minor skin angiofibroma > collagenoma > lipoma; benign adreno-cortical adenoma (m/c), meningioma (m/c neuro), pheo <1%; malignant PNET, thymic & foregut carcinoid.

units.title: MEN1 organ-by-organ and the MEN2A gene
units.guide: 1° HPT: MEN1 asymmetric hyperplasia <20 yrs M=F vs sporadic adenoma F>40 (peak 60); IOC 99mTc sestamibi; Rx 3½ near-total parathyroidectomy. m/c hypercalcaemia symptom = fatigue. Pancreas: enteropancreatic NET = m/c cause of death; gastrinoma > insulinoma > glucagonoma (migratory necrolytic erythematous rash) > VIPoma (WDHA, NAGMA). Gastrinoma MEN1: duodenum, small multifocal, <5%, endoscopic US, lymph; sporadic: Passaro's, large, >50–60%, SRS, blood; >2 cm surgery; streptozocin+octreotide vs high-dose PPI. Pituitary prolactinoma aggressive macro. MEN2A = RET (10q, point mutation).

units.title: MEN2A variants, MEN2B/MEN3 and MEN4
units.guide: Classical MEN2A: MTC 100% + pheo 50% + parathyroid hyperplasia 25%; variants + cutaneous lichen amyloidosis, + Hirschsprung's, FMTC. MEN2B/3: MTC 100% + pheo 50% + marfanoid habitus, mucosal & intestinal ganglioneuromatosis (tongue photo), myelinated corneal nerves. MEN4 = CDKN1B: parathyroid + pituitary + renal/adrenal + testicular/ovarian tumours.

units.title: Syndrome gene table and Carney's triad
units.guide: HPT-jaw tumour (parafibromin/CDC73; ossifying jaw fibroma; parathyroid Ca), Carney's complex (PRKAR1A; atrial myxoma lepidic; PPNAD thin Cushing's, GH adenoma; lentigenes), VHL (Chr3; RCC, cerebellar haemangioblastoma, islet tumours, papillary cystadenoma broad ligament, epididymal cyst, endolymphatic sac; pheo; pancreatic cysts), NF1 (Chr17; optic sheath > meningioma; pheo U/L), Cowden (PTEN; breast Ca, hamartomatous polyps; nodular goitre/Hashimoto's), McCune-Albright (not inherited, post-zygotic GNAS; PFD, precocious puberty, café-au-lait). Carney's triad = pulmonary chondroma + GIST + paraganglioma.

units.title: RCC comparisons, Cushing's by age and the APS 1/2 table
units.guide: VHL RCC B/L young lymphatic vs sporadic U/L elderly blood-stream. TS: kidney cysts + angiomyolipoma vs VHL pancreatic cysts (m/c) + RCC. Cushing's m/c cause: adults pituitary adenoma; infants McCune-Albright; toddlers adrenocortical carcinoma. PGA = APS: type 1 childhood M=F AR, APECED/AIRE, anti-21-hydroxylase + anti-interferon, skin/nail +, Graves > Hashimoto's + hypoparathyroidism + Addison's, candidiasis; type 2 adult F>M polygenic HLA DR3/DR4, Hashimoto's > Graves + Addison's, coeliac association; minor both type 1 DM + hypogonadism.
